method_note: Read the whole target. Picked claims with the highest impact on a test oracle: RFC section numbers and the q-value rule, JSON-LD 1.1 sections 6.1/6.2/7, ACT/UNTP/W3C VC render status, ESPR/Batteries/toys/detergents article numbers, GitHub repository metadata (gh api), the renderer Accept lists in source code, DOIs and venues (Crossref/OpenAlex/Zenodo), and the existing_check mappings against the local engine source. WebFetch summarises with a small model, so legal and RFC claims were read in chunks and only counted as confirmed when the chunk showed the point. WCAG 2.2, ePrivacy Art. 5(3), EAA Art. 2 and the m01/m07 prior-record claims were not re-checked.

checked.claim: RFC 9110 sections: 8.7 Content-Location, 9.3.2 HEAD, 12.1 proactive, 12.2 reactive, 12.4.2 quality values, 12.5.1 Accept, 12.5.4 Accept-Language, 12.5.5 Vary, 15.4.1 300, 15.4.4 303, 15.5.7 406, 15.5.11 410.
checked.evidence: The table of contents lists each of these numbers with the same titles.

checked.claim: Weight q is 0 to 1, default 1, q=0 means not acceptable, at most three decimals.
checked.evidence: Section 12.4.2: real number 0 to 1, 0.001 least preferred, 0 not acceptable, default 1, a sender must not write more than three digits after the point. Note the limit binds senders; a server oracle should still tolerate longer input.

checked.claim: When no representation matches, a server may send a default representation or answer 406.
checked.evidence: Section 12.1 says a server may send a response that ignores the stated preferences instead of 406, and may not support proactive negotiation for a resource at all.

checked.claim: RFC 9111: 4.1 Vary cache keys, 3.5 authenticated responses, 5.2.2.1 max-age, 5.2.2.4 no-cache, 5.2.2.5 no-store, 5.2.2.7 private, 5.2.2.9 public; STD 98, obsoletes RFC 7234, June 2022.
checked.evidence: Headings and header block match; public marks a response as cacheable.

checked.claim: Only one Link header with the json-ld#context relation is allowed, and it is ignored for application/ld+json.
checked.evidence: Section 6.1 text: at most one such header; for application/ld+json the linked context is ignored.

checked.claim: 6.2 alternate Link with type application/ld+json; section 7 embeds JSON-LD in script elements; 7.1 base, 7.2 restrictions, 7.3 fragment selection; unselected script blocks merge into one dataset.
checked.evidence: Section titles match. 6.2 uses rel alternate with type application/ld+json. 7.3: a fragment equal to a script id selects that block alone; otherwise all blocks merge, with shared blank node identifiers.

checked.claim: Edition and date of JSON-LD 1.1 were not re-checked.
checked.evidence: The page is a W3C Recommendation of 16 July 2020, this version https://www.w3.org/TR/2020/REC-json-ld11-20200716/.
checked.correction: Fill the gap: W3C Recommendation, 16 July 2020.

checked.claim: W3C Recommendation 5 February 2026; outcomes passed, failed, inapplicable, cantTell, untested.
checked.evidence: Recommendation of 5 February 2026 by the Accessibility Guidelines WG; version URL matches; the five outcome names match.

checked.claim: UNTP VC page is Work in Progress, renderMethod is a SHOULD, RenderTemplate2024 kept from 0.7.0, mediaType text/html, digestMultibase SHA-256 multihash base64url.
checked.evidence: Page labelled Work in Progress with 0.7.0 and 0.6.0 listed; renderMethod SHOULD; RenderTemplate2024 retained from 0.7.0; hosted templates set mediaType text/html; version 1.0 expected after public review.

checked.claim: Editor's copy, self-described experimental, SuiteRenderMethod with summary, html, static suites; digestMultibase prefix u with SHA-256.
checked.evidence: Page says experimental and not fit for production; SuiteRenderMethod and three suites match; digestMultibase uses prefix u and SHA-2 256 multihash. The html suite runs in a sandboxed iframe, which matters if the engine ever meets it.

checked.claim: ESPR Art. 2(28) passport reachable through a data carrier; Art. 2(30) unique product identifier allows a web link.
checked.evidence: Point 28 is the digital product passport (accessible electronically through a data carrier), point 29 the data carrier, point 30 the unique product identifier that enables a web link.
checked.correction: Where the file cites 'data carrier' alone, the definition is Art. 2(29); Art. 2(28) is the passport definition.

checked.claim: identifier.resolve takes accept and accepted_media_types; a non-accepted final media type gives IDENTIFIER.RESPONSE.MEDIA_TYPE; 404/410 give IDENTIFIER.UNRESOLVED.

checked.evidence: Route regex has the .html suffix; resolve returns 303 with Location /dpp/{ident}; only do_GET found; no Vary or Cache-Control string; view() writes <html lang="en"> and <th scope="row">; FAULTS contains the three named flags and no negotiation, HEAD or cookie fault.

checked.claim: Last change commit of reference_server.py and reference-system.md is ed5779c (2026-10-18).
checked.evidence: ed5779c exists (2026-10-18 17:05, 'fix: apply adapter review check findings') and touched the file, but 'git log' on the current branch lists f743f5a ('bind the resolved passport to the API item target') as the newest commit touching reference_server.py; its author date is earlier, so the order is by topology. The claim 'last change' is not clearly right.

checked.claim: access.restricted_fields reads the html channel for leaks; identifier.parse accepts http as well as https.

The file's remark that HTML has no entitlement rule is consistent with the capability text (entitled fields are checked on the fetch channel).

checked.evidence: Art. 31(2): Member States apply the measures from 28 June 2025; 31(3) lets them apply Art. 4(8) obligations up to 28 June 2027. Art. 2(1),(2) scope text was not in the chunk I read, so the 'not listed' claim stays unchecked.

checked.claim_ref: layers.L04 specs and regulatory_alignment (Batteries Art. 77(5) 'structured and searchable')
checked.claim: Art. 77(5) adds structured and searchable data.
checked.evidence: The chunk summary of Art. 77(5) names open standards, interoperable, machine-readable and transferable without vendor lock-in, and did not mention 'searchable'. Not refuted: the summariser may have dropped the word.
checked.correction: Re-read the exact wording of Art. 77(5) before the L04 claim and the law_delta ('asks for searchable data') are used.

missed_items.fact: JSON-LD 1.1 is a W3C Recommendation dated 16 July 2020; the target left this blank.
ESPR Art. 2(29) defines the data carrier as a machine-readable medium such as a linear barcode or two-dimensional symbol; 2(28) is the passport and 2(30) the unique product identifier.

Under Art. 13(6) Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, the QR code from 18 February 2027 links to the passport only for LMT, industrial over 2 kWh and EV batteries; other batteries link to labelling and conformity information, so a carrier test must not demand a passport for all batteries.

The operator must give dealers and online platforms a digital copy of the carrier or identifier, or a web link, free and within five working days of a request. The target cites 10(3) without the five-day rule, which an engine could test as a process check.
The three-decimal limit applies to senders (clients), so the negotiation matrix should send at most three digits and treat longer values from other clients as a tolerance question, not a fault.

The W3C render-method html suite is specified to run in a sandboxed iframe with CSP and no network access, which matches the engine rule not to execute HTML; an engine could only check the declared digest, not the output.

overall: The file is largely reliable. All 26 claims I could check against primary sources held: RFC and JSON-LD section numbers, the q-value rule, ESPR, Batteries, toys and detergent article numbers, repository licences and release data, renderer Accept strings in source code, DOIs, and the engine check mappings (identifier.resolve codes, reference-server behaviour). Two items stay unconfirmed: the 'last change commit ed5779c' for the reference server, and the word 'searchable' in Batteries Art. 77(5). Small corrections are needed for axe-core's push date, missing venues for three DOIs, the JSON-LD edition, and the battery QR-code target. No protected-standard paraphrase was found; ISO/IEC 15459, EN 301 549 and ISO/IEC 40500 are only named. I did not re-check WCAG 2.2 criteria, ePrivacy Art. 5(3), EAA Art. 2 or the claims taken from prior records m01 and m07.
